novelty_flags.one_line: They attribute the common-menu conditional-iid inequality result to “Theorem 2.3,” but in the cited July-2025 NBER version 2.3 is a Condition and the result is Theorem 2.4.

soundness_flags.label: ass:absolute-continuity
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited Mbakop source assumes conditional continuous distributions, not absolute continuity with respect to Lebesgue measure on the full utility-shock vector; weaken the condition or retag and justify the stronger restriction.

source_verification_receipts.version: NBER Working Paper 29025, July 2025 revision (rev0 PDF)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Condition 2.3 supplies the comparison premise; Theorem 2.4 supplies the conditional probability inequalities. There is no Theorem 2.3 carrying that claim.
The manuscript requires shocks to be “continuously distributed” and separately defines conditional iid; it does not state Lebesgue absolute continuity of the conditional law on R^J.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Correct every Pakes theorem anchor to Theorem 2.4, quote its common-choice-universe premise, and state precisely which changing-menu step prevents its direct use.

Replace full-vector absolute continuity by the weakest no-ties/continuous-shock condition needed for the patch construction, or label absolute continuity as a stronger maintained condition and give an empirical justification.

Make the finite-menu layer more than a generic fallback by stating a certified enumeration/optimization complexity bound and a worked four-plan certificate that separates the grid method from generic polynomial optimization.

recommended_next_step: Revise the two citation/assumption defects, then advance the repaired field-tier terminal-frontier and three-plan analytic-body kernel to Stage 0.
